hints.content:
Veronica is trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the number of animals per $1$ kilometer.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{animals}}}{\maroonD{\text{distance (km)}}} = \purpleD{\text{animals per kilometer}}$

If we write each unit rate as a decimal, we can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

Let's see what Veronica did instead.

###Finding the unit rates

Hike| $\blueE{\text{Number of}}$ $\blueE{\text{animals seen}} $ || $\maroonD{\text{Length of}}$ $\maroonD{\text{hike}}$||Number of $\purpleD{\text{animals seen per kilometer}}$
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Rivers Edge  |$8$|$\div$ | $3$|$\approx$|$2.7$
Wooded Marsh|$24$ |$\div$ |$8$ | $=$|$3$
Canyon Creek |$35$ |$\div$ | $15$|$\approx$| $2.3$

Veronica did not divide by the length of the hike. So she compared the total numbers of animals instead of the unit rates she wanted.

###The mistake

Veronica ordered by number of animals instead of by animals per kilometer.

question.content:
Veronica went on three hikes. On each hike, she saw the following numbers of animals:

Hike | Length of hike $(\text{km})$| Number of animals seen 
- | :-: | :-:
Rivers Edge | $3$| $8$ 
Wooded Marsh| $8$ | $24$ 
Canyon Creek| $15$ | $35$ 

Veronica tried to order the hikes from least to greatest by *number of animals seen per kilometer*, but she made a mistake. Here's her work:

$\stackrel{\text{Least}}{\underbrace{8}_\text{River's Edge}} < \underbrace{24}_\text{Wooded Marsh} < \stackrel{\text{Greatest}}{\underbrace{35}_\text{Canyon Creek}}$

**What was Veronica's mistake?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: Veronica calculated kilometers per animal instead of animals per kilometer.
Veronica ordered by number of animals instead of by animals per kilometer.
Veronica ordered from greatest to least instead of least to greatest.
